title: The republic that bought its freedom
episode: The History of Dubrovnik & The Republic of Ragusa
description: A half-hour history of Dubrovnik, from refugees founding a town on a rocky islet in the 600s to the Republic of Ragusa, which paid tribute to stronger powers and traded with all of them. Pile Gate is the main entrance on the west.

title: A walk on the walls, and a few cats
episode: Dubrovnik - history, sieges, captures, liberations, and staring cats
description: Lindybeige, a British history YouTuber, walks the walls and explains how the city kept its freedom for centuries and why the defenses look as they do. The round Minčeta Tower, finished in 1464, is the highest point of the walls.

title: Salt harvested by hand since the Middle Ages
episode: The Salt of Ston: Local Stories Ep 11
description: A salt worker at Ston, about an hour up the coast, where seawater is still dried in shallow pans and raked by hand. Salt made Ragusa rich, and the republic built miles of walls across the peninsula to protect the pans.

title: The oysters of Mali Ston Bay
episode: The future of Mali Ston’s famous oysters
description: A short film on the native flat oysters farmed in Mali Ston Bay, where fresh water from springs meets the sea, and on the growers worried about warming water. People in Dubrovnik drive up for them in spring.

title: The earthquake of 1667
description: An animation from the Dubrovnik Museums of the earthquake of April 6, 1667, which destroyed most of the city and killed thousands, including the rector. The Baroque churches and houses seen today were mostly built afterward.

title: Dalmatia’s close-harmony singing
episode: Klapa multipart singing of Dalmatia, southern Croatia
description: UNESCO’s film on klapa, the unaccompanied singing of small groups, traditionally men, heard along the Dalmatian coast in squares, taverns, and churches. In summer, groups often sing in the old town’s squares and courtyards.

title: News footage of the siege
episode: Siege of Dubrovnik | Shocking Footage of City Under Fire | Croatian War of Independence (1991)
description: Reports by ITN, a British news service, from Dubrovnik in late 1991, as the Yugoslav army shelled the city from the hills and the sea. Hundreds of the old town’s buildings were hit, and the world watched the damage on television.

title: The feast held under siege
episode: Dubrovnik u Ratu-Festa Sv Vlaha 1992, Feast of St Blaise Dubrovnik 1992
description: Footage of the feast of St. Blaise, the city’s patron saint, on February 3, 1992, when Dubrovnik was still cut off by the Yugoslav army. The procession has been held every year for more than 1,000 years, and it went ahead.

title: The hilltop fort that held
episode: War Relics of the FORGOTTEN RIDGE: The Hill That Saved Dubrovnik 1991/1992
description: The battle for Mount Srđ, the ridge above the city. On December 6, 1991, a small group of defenders in Fort Imperial, built by Napoleon’s army, held off an assault. The fort now houses a museum of the war.

title: King’s Landing on location
episode: Game of Thrones  On Location in Croatia HBO
description: HBO’s short film on shooting Game of Thrones in Dubrovnik, which played King’s Landing from the second season on. The Baroque Jesuit Stairs were the setting for Cersei’s walk of atonement in the fifth season.

title: A city crowded by its own success
episode: Croatian city of Dubrovnik overwhelmed by mass tourism
description: A news report on the crowds that fill the old town in summer, from cruise passengers and Game of Thrones fans, and on how residents have moved out as houses became rentals. Pile Gate is where most visitors enter.
